scores.proposal_name: NEGATIVE SPACE: a cut-paper noir where the extra guest is the hole
scores.strengths:
The direction most tightly bound to the screenplay's own logic. Its single doctrine (paper world over a hidden backing-ember lightbox, so the Extra can only subtract, cutting holes onto the fire to come) unites the counting horror and the climax: the explosion's negative frames are literally the Extra's material, and the final warm hand is made of firelight. That gives 'Two.' the right double charge of relief and dread. Many design choices are motivated by specific lines:
- Deena's high ponytail is what gets gripped, which pays off Scott's 'I saw her hair--'.
- The handprint is a hole beside Deena, which fits Angelo's 'I was right there.'
- The second CLICK is dry and panned to Scott's right.
- The misregistered ring of seven piles against six chairs.
- The hand circle as a pentagon with four bodies.
- The fifth whip pan lands on the empty chair.
- Christof's dead joke shows as marquee bulbs that fail to light.
- Angelo's silhouette sheds its signatures one by one (jacket over Deena, cigarette dropped, only the lighter left), the clearest visual telling of his sacrifice in any proposal.
- The letterbox squeezes until the frame is a slit holding two men and a lighter.
- Scott's type goes ash after the fire and returns to tungsten on 'Two.'
Silhouette is also the most robust answer to the procedural-face risk. The sound design is precise: vacuum silences, the 7th-harmonic leitmotif, and a groove that turns to 7/8.
scores.weaknesses:
Silhouettes put the friendships' warmth and the Scott/Kay 'almost a question' at risk. Profiles with no interior features cannot carry Deena's 'eyes fix on Angelo, disbelieving' or Angelo's smile draining unless the eight graphic-eye ECUs are spent deliberately. The Kay subplot is under-designed (no through-line for the Saturday text).

Over-signalling:
- The letterbox steps on Kay's bathroom click, which tells the audience she is gone long before anyone notices. That spoils the later 'six people apparently playing' ambiguity.
- That beat is missing from the key sequences entirely.

VOICE type logic is muddled. Setting 'Scott.' in Scott's own face reads as Scott saying his own name.

Palette crowding:
- Scott's tungsten (#F2A93B) sits too close to the Extra's ember (#FF9440).
- Four nearby reds: Deena crimson, Kay lipstick, wine, blood.

Continuity errors:
- The 'only Kay came in from the rain' footprint clue contradicts its own rainy arrivals.
- The ending's call timer reads 00:01:12 before the call connects.
- The timer must reach 02:51 within an 80-second sequence, yet it is billed as the one thing that never jumps.

At 14 minutes and about 150 shots it is heavy. Holding a 2.76 slit while dialogue plays creates a type-space conflict.

scores.proposal_name: RECOUNT: the night, rebuilt as evidence
scores.strengths:
It has the single best emotional typography idea in the set. Scott's lines are typed with a caret and deleted backwards like the text he started on Monday and never sent, and 'Two.' is the only Scott line never deleted. That ties the Kay subplot straight to the ending.

Other strong ideas:
- Angelo's cards fly, then drop, then land face-down and flip after Deena dies. At 'Scott. Please.' there is no card at all, exactly on the script's 'first time all night he hasn't sounded like himself.'
- Kay's 'Big night for you.' lingers at 8% on the corridor wall until the procession passes the bathroom door.
- Marina's last wine ring hangs in the empty doorway with no text.
- The gas hiss is planted subliminally from the moment Christof leaves the table.
- Missing-time void frames.
- The 'clean after a house fire' final hand is a chilling detail.
- The truthful HEADCOUNT drop for Marina while everyone watches Angelo hold Deena is a genuinely nasty scare.
scores.weaknesses:
It imposes a forensic frame the screenplay never has: no investigation exists, and the story is Scott's intimate, subjective night. Evidence tents, measurement callouts ('SUBJECT DISTANCE ≈ 2.6 m'), a 'SPEAKER: UNATTRIBUTED' tag and eight exhibit freezes over-explain the mystery, halt momentum at peak moments and cool the grief into a puzzle box.

The always-true death counter is a morbid scoreboard. It announces Kay's death three seconds after the door clicks, killing the slow dawning that drives Act 2. The 'record = visible + 1' rules game also makes the Extra a countable person, which flattens the ambiguity.

It reads the handprint as Marina's (ring gaps), but she vanished at the door, not beside Deena, and the script's horror is 'I was right there.'

It is the hardest to build well:
- mouthless procedural faces with 3-view crossfades;
- stroke-rig hands that risk looking like rubber gloves;
- formant 'voice-ghosts' that risk game babble.
This is exactly the uncanny or cheap risk the brief warns against. The six-face 22% overprint for the VOICE is conceptually neat but muddy to read.

scores.proposal_name: ONE ROD TOO MANY: a shadow theatre for seven
scores.strengths:
It has the most original counting grammar: the N+1 rod rule and a persistent scrim whose holes accumulate, so the VOICE's letters stay burned into the room and light the lighter standoff 'like stars'. It also has several emotionally intelligent ideas:
- Kay animated on ones, the way Scott sees her. After the bathroom, glimpses of 'Kay' snap on twos: something else is wearing her timing.
- The VOICE borrows the face of the person it echoes (the first 'Scott.' in Angelo's face before he says it), the smartest reading of 'a perfectly familiar voice'.
- Christof's ribbon line stays pinned to his empty chair, his biscuit stays on the table, and the ending's count is cut as left-behind objects.
- Christof folded at every split pin like a paper doll in an envelope: hard-hitting and non-gory.
- A second heartbeat drifts into lockstep with Scott's and lands on 'Two.'
- Scott's letters narrow with dread and release on 'Two.', each casting two shadows.
- The 38-second unbroken take for the lighter standoff.
scores.weaknesses:
The meta puppet-theatre frame makes every friend literally a puppet on a stick. Brass split pins, hinged jaws flapping as text reveals, and plates under every line (tissue strips, cards, vellum, ribbons, coasters) push the tone toward folkloric charm and away from the relentless intensity the user asked for.

The bare rod is visible from frame one, so the Extra's presence is announced rather than felt.

The rod logic conflates leaving the stage with dying, since Kay's rod drops when she simply walks off frame.

The rod from above that jerks Deena's head gives the Extra a visible instrument.

Requiring every wide to show the stage lip constrains the cinematography for 12 minutes, and the rods add constant clutter. The Shepard-tone rise is a stock device.

winner: NEGATIVE SPACE: a cut-paper noir where the extra guest is the hole
grafts: From RECOUNT: Scott's unsent-text caret. A thin tungsten caret blinks after Scott's unfinished lines and in his silences with Kay: between them at the door ('almost a question'), after 'What about Saturday?', and on 'I--' in the cold open. Cut to black on the 7th blink. Keep NEGATIVE SPACE's guillotine for interruptions. 'Two.' is the one Scott line with no caret and no exit: it stays until the fade. This gives the Scott/Kay thread a visual through-line to the ending.

From ONE ROD: Kay alone animates on ones while everyone else is on twos (she is more alive to Scott). After the bathroom click, every partial glimpse of 'Kay' at the later game snaps on twos with Scott-unfamiliar timing. Something else is wearing her timing. This slots straight into NEGATIVE SPACE's 12 fps rig cadence at no cost.

From ONE ROD: replace 'VOICE borrows the face of the name it says' with 'VOICE borrows the face of the person it is echoing'. The first 'Scott.' is in Angelo's Oswald, since Angelo will close the round with 'Scott.'. The soft 'Angelo.' is in Deena's Archivo Black, her own 'Angelo.' from the seven-hands stop. Keep it as a knockout to backing-ember.

From ONE ROD: VOICE knockout letters do not vanish on the cut. They stay as faint burnt-in perforations in the dining-room paper (the table plane and wall) in every later shot of that room, slowly brightening. By the lighter standoff the accumulated cuts (letters, the throat line, the handprint) leak ember into the dark. This fits the lightbox doctrine perfectly.

From ONE ROD: a second, quieter heartbeat enters under the ending call, out of phase with Scott's, and its period drifts into exact lockstep on 'Two.' Use it alongside or instead of the two-sine unison.

From RECOUNT and ONE ROD: save Angelo's full break for 'Scott. Please.', the script's 'first time all night he hasn't sounded like himself'. Before that, his dealing decays: words land crooked, then drop rather than fly. From 'Scott. Please.' on he switches to lighter-cream Oswald 300, undealt, with no landing sound. His very last line, 'Sorry about your house.', is one final card dealt face-down that flips over 18 frames: the poor magician's last trick.

From RECOUNT: Kay's 'Big night for you.' leaves a faint afterimage (about 8%) on the corridor wall in every later hallway shot. It dies on the exact frame Scott's hand stops short of the bathroom handle.
From RECOUNT: Marina's full stops are already tiny wine rings in NEGATIVE SPACE. Her last ring hangs alone, empty of text, in the empty kitchen-doorway rectangle when she is gone.

From ONE ROD: left-behind objects. Christof's biscuit stays on the table and his last marquee line 'And don't touch my cards.' stays dimly lit (bulbs at 20%) over his empty place when the bottle arrives. In the ending count, cut one insert per name (Deena's hoop, Christof's biscuit, Angelo's dropped cigarette, Kay's lip-marked glass, Marina's ring glints). These cuts shuffle out of order as the numbers 'won't stay still', combined with NEGATIVE SPACE's orbit of names and the sixth letterless knockout slot.

From RECOUNT: plant the gas hiss subliminally (-54 dBFS) on the frame Christof walks into the kitchen and ramp it about 2 dB per minute, instead of starting it at the kitchen entrance. It rewards a second viewing and builds unexplained pressure.

From ONE ROD: play the lighter standoff as one unbroken 30-40 s slow push, ending on Angelo's thumb, with the continuous letterbox squeeze happening inside that single take. The film's first long take, after a kitchen cut at about 1.3 s ASL, lands harder than 7-9 s holds.

From ONE ROD: Christof in the oven is folded at the paper joints into an impossible flat stack, with crease lines across the crushed side of the curl cloud. Keep NEGATIVE SPACE's projected ceiling shadow as the first image.
From ONE ROD: party walla and laughter as a synthesized murmur bed. On 'Maybe you don't get to play.' the laugh starts and cuts off a beat too early, so the room's warmth audibly fails.
From RECOUNT: lock the runtime with a type-only animatic (every verbatim line at its hold time) before any art. With no voices, the type's reading speed is the film's pacing.
must_fix:
Do not spoil Kay. Remove the letterbox step on the bathroom-door click. Tie each matte step to the moment an absence is felt or noticed:
- Kay's step on 'Where's Kay?'
- Christof's on the crash.
- Deena's on her last breath.
- Marina's on the empty doorway.
The audience should dawn with Scott, not be told.

Add the missing 'LATER' table beat ('Six piles now. Six people apparently playing.'). It is a core dread moment. Stage 'Kay' only in fragments: a rain-bead hair edge behind a shoulder, out of focus behind a glass, cropped at frame edge, moving on twos (see the graft). Never give her a clean view, and never let the lip-marked glass move.

Lock one seating plan for every table scene and make the Extra's gap coincide with the chair Kay asked Scott to 'Save my seat'. Then the seventh pile, the sixth card, 'Kay' at the later game, the fifth wineglass, the empty roll-call corner and the photographer's spot all sit in one coherent place, at Scott's right.

Separate the Extra's colour from Scott's. Tungsten #F2A93B and backing-ember #FF9440 are too close, and the knockout 'Scott.' could read as Scott's own type. Make knockout read as a hole, not a colour: hotter value, live fire-noise flicker inside the letters, halation, no grain, a cut-paper edge. Consider shifting Scott's type cooler or paler. Likewise, make Deena's crimson and Kay's lipstick clearly distinct in hue and value, with wine and blood kept darker.

Fix the call-timer continuity:
- The timer cannot run before the call connects (it reads 00:01:12 during the missed dialling).
- If it is 'the only thing that counts correctly', it must not jump: the ending's on-screen time from connect to 'Two.' must match 02:51, or the timer must be off-screen across any elision.
- Clear the cold-open loop interpretation (cold open happens after 'Two.') with the author before building it.

Correct the footprint clue. All guests arrived through rain, so 'only Kay came in from the rain' is false inside the film's own arrivals. Use prints that match no arrival: an extra pair beyond the count, or prints that begin inside the threshold.

Keep the ending ambiguous and let the relief land first. The final hand must read first as Scott's sudden, aching relief (warmth on his face, shoulders dropping, 'Two.' returning to tungsten) before the wide shows no figure. Make the handprint-to-final-hand rhyme a second-viewing echo (similar, not a highlighted identical path with a flicker callout), so the Kay reading ('Save my seat', 'Big night for you') stays alive beside the horror reading.

Reserve dialogue space inside the 2.20-2.76 letterbox. Specify where the standoff and kitchen lines sit: inside the slit at reduced but legible size, or set onto the matte itself. Keep the 44 px minimum and the hold-time rule even at the tightest aspect ratio.

Budget the runtime realistically. About 150 shots across 14 masters is a lot for code. Identify which shots are reuses of master set-ups, and protect Act 1's comic timing (arrivals and party) from being compressed, since the losses only hurt if the friendships land first.

scores.proposal_name: NEGATIVE SPACE: a cut-paper noir where the extra guest is the hole
scores.strengths: This is the only direction that turns the brief's two biggest technical risks into style choices. Silhouettes mean there are no faces to go uncanny. Overlapping limbs merge in one ink, so simple 14-joint rigs look seamless. The shared library of about 16 silhouette hand poses can reach a premium finish, while shaded procedural hands cannot. Fire is designed as flat three-tone flame plus embers, not simulated particle soup. Posterised three-band light, cut-paper edge noise, rim crescents, grain and gate weave give a premium look that one engine can repeat across about 150 shots from 14 master set-ups. The Extra rule (subtraction only: knockouts to an ember lightbox, gaps in the composition, actions only across cuts) fits the script's 'No second figure is visible'. It is also cheap to build: destination-out on one layer. The letterbox closing one step per loss is a strong, almost free intensity device. The second CLICK played dry and panned to Scott's right, the groove gaining a seventh beat, vacuum silences, and the 7th-harmonic leitmotif (correctly 31 cents flat) give a rising tension curve. Using the same right-hand path for the handprint and the final hand is the best horror payoff of the three proposals. The phone photo can be re-rendered for free because it comes from the same renderer. Type behaviours are distinct per character and come with explicit hold-time and lines-on-screen rules.
scores.weaknesses:
Story deviations:
- The script says 'Six hands come down on six cards.' The proposal shows five hands and a card that flattens under nothing, which would make the characters' lack of reaction implausible.
- The hand-circle 'pentagon' contradicts 'He is holding Angelo's hand. Of course he is.'
- The later beat ('Six piles now. Six people apparently playing... Kay not visible in any clear view') is never actually staged. It also conflicts with the never-a-positive-shape doctrine.
- VOICE lines set in the named person's own face ('Scott.' in Scott's type) read as that person saying their own name.

Act 1 risk: about five minutes of comic banter from six faceless black shapes could feel cold and hard to tell apart in wide shots.

Type contrast: tungsten, ivory and silver type will disappear over tungsten light bands unless it is restricted to ink areas.

Technical gaps:
- Damped springs are stateful, which breaks render(t).
- Path2D cannot be flattened for the edge noise.
- Canvas 2D has no 'threshold' operation for halation.
- One 14-minute OfflineAudioContext is about 320 MB.
- The 1.3 s kitchen average shot length conflicts with the dialogue hold rule unless lines can carry across cuts.
- Keypad dialling while the call timer shows 00:01:12 is a continuity error.
- A full-width ember line across a profile neck silhouette reads as decapitation.

scores.proposal_name: RECOUNT: the night, rebuilt as evidence
scores.strengths:
The best dialogue thinking of the three:
- Scott types with a caret and deletes backwards. This comes straight from the unsent Saturday text, and 'Two.' is the only line he never deletes.
- Angelo's lines are card slugs that go face-down and then stop altogether.
- Kay's lines condense like breath on glass.
- Marina's lines plot onto a baseline with wine rings, and her last ring hangs in the empty doorway.
- The Dispatcher is a transcript that never changes, with Scott's address shown as redaction bars.
- Background banter is drawn as out-of-focus type behind the main exchange.

It is faithful to 'Six hands come down on six cards', showing a sixth hand whose arm fades into the dark. UK craft details are accurate (DTMF tones, ringback cadence, 999). Strong sound ideas: the gas hiss creeping in subliminally from the moment Christof leaves, count ticks that drift flat, and audio rendered per scene. It handles determinism with care: closed-form particles, hair driven by a convolution of past head motion, and quarter-resolution halation. The HEADCOUNT odometer is a powerful dramatic-irony engine.
scores.weaknesses:
The weakest direction to build at premium quality:
- Full-colour, shaded procedural faces in three views with crossfades at the turn thresholds will pop and look like Flash cut-outs.
- Mouthless faces with eye glints may look like mannequins in the comedy first act.
- Skin-toned hands built from 15 joints with creases and nails are the exact 'rubber glove' risk the proposal itself names.
- The fire is value-noise (fbm) upscaled from 320x180, which looks like a screensaver.
- Per-shape gradients, blurred contact shadows and 2.5D projection for every shot is a large build.
- Formant 'voice-ghosts' for 249 lines risk sounding like game beep-speech.

The story suffers too. The truthful HEADCOUNT, the red delta flags, black void frames, 'SPEAKER: UNATTRIBUTED' tags and eight halftone exhibit freezes over-explain the mystery: they declare Kay dead three seconds after the bathroom click and count the Extra as a living person. That collapses ambiguity the script deliberately keeps. The freezes also break momentum in exactly the stretch that needs relentless pacing. It also contradicts itself: 'Kay' is shown as a red sleeve after Rule Zero says the Extra has no body.

scores.proposal_name: ONE ROD TOO MANY: a shadow theatre for seven
scores.strengths:
Rods counting one more than the puppets on stage (N+1) is a genuinely new counting grammar, and close-ups that crop the stage edge are a smart place to hide the vanishings. Profile-only puppets with eye holes are very buildable, and one rig per character keeps the cast consistent.

Strong individual ideas:
- A persistent scrim that collects every hole the Extra cuts, so the room leaks more light as the film goes on.
- The VOICE punched through the paper in the typeface of the person it is imitating ('Scott.' in Angelo's face, said before Angelo says it).
- Kay's distinctive timing, with the fake 'Kay' later moving on the wrong cadence.
- A 38-second unbroken standoff take after rapid cutting.
- A second heartbeat that drifts into lockstep on 'Two.'
- A deterministic burn-through mask at low resolution for the explosion.
- Left-behind objects: the biscuit, the pinned line on the chair, Marina's ring.
scores.weaknesses: The puppet-theatre frame distances the audience: visible rods, brass split pins, the stage lip and puppeteer blackouts read as charming and folkloric, which works against the relentless intensity the user asked for. The rods also add a meta layer (who holds them?) that the story does not have. Hinged jaws that flap while text reveals will read as comic lip-flap. Readability fails at speed: Marina's lines wrapped around a coaster circle and Christof's curved baselines are hard to read in a dialogue-heavy film. Every line sits on a plate (strips, cards, coasters, vellum), which clutters the frame and looks like a visual novel. Caveat looks cheap. The '[ADDRESS]' placeholder looks like a template bug. Holes 'accumulating' across rooms does not make sense spatially (the dining-room scrim versus the kitchen). Rods in every wide add constant clutter.

winner: NEGATIVE SPACE: a cut-paper noir where the extra guest is the hole
grafts: From ONE ROD TOO MANY: the VOICE takes the typeface of the person whose line it is mimicking, not the face of the name it says. 'Scott.' is a knockout in Angelo's Oswald, so Angelo's real 'Scott.' lands as an echo and 'I just did.' stings. The soft 'Angelo.' is a knockout in Scott's Franklin, echoing Scott's opening line of round two. Keep NEGATIVE SPACE's ember knockout, single-frame cut-on and digital silence.

From ONE ROD TOO MANY: knockout damage persists. Each set keeps a list of the Extra's knockout paths (VOICE letters, the handprint), and they stay faintly glowing ember whenever that master set-up returns, so the house leaks more lightbox as the film goes on. Keep it per set so the geography stays coherent.
From ONE ROD TOO MANY: in the ending, a second lub-dub heartbeat, panned to Scott's right and out of phase, drifts in period until it locks exactly with Scott's on 'Two.', under the two-sine unison.

From ONE ROD TOO MANY: timing as identity. Kay keeps her slow 1.25x easing. After the bathroom CLICK, any fragment of 'Kay' at the later game (rain-bead glints, the lip-marked glass being set down) moves on the wrong cadence: single-frame jumps between cuts. Something else is wearing her.

From ONE ROD TOO MANY: play the lighter standoff as one unbroken take of about 50-55 s, from the lighter coming out to the failed spark: a slow push, with the letterbox squeezing from 2.39 to 2.76 as the only thing that changes. The first cut after the kitchen's 1.3 s rhythm is Scott running.

From ONE ROD TOO MANY: the burn-through technique. Compute a deterministic fractal-noise threshold mask at 480x270 with an ember band and a char band, then upscale it. Use it for the cold-open curtain and for the letterbox mattes burning away in the explosion.

From ONE ROD TOO MANY / RECOUNT: the extra blank card. Whenever the count is wrong, Angelo's dealt row of words gets one more dealt slot at the end: an empty, card-width gap with a card snap. It is never acknowledged.

From RECOUNT: Scott's caret. His lines type on with a 2 px caret (the text he started on Monday and never sent) and leave by deleting backwards. Keep the guillotined dashes for interruptions. The cold open cuts on the caret's seventh blink. 'Me.' and 'Two.' type slowly, and 'Two.' is the only Scott line in the film that is never deleted.
From RECOUNT: Kay's 'Big night for you.' stays as a faint afterimage on the corridor wall in later hallway shots and is gone on the exact frame Scott's hand stops short of the bathroom handle.
From RECOUNT: when Marina vanishes, her last gold ring-shaped full stop is left hanging alone in the empty doorway rectangle, with no text, before Scott's 'Marina?' floats in.

From RECOUNT: start the gas hiss subliminally, at about -54 dBFS, the moment Christof goes to the kitchen (when the knobs are broken), and raise it about 2 dB a minute without explanation until 'What's that smell?'.
From RECOUNT: count ticks that sour. Each count ping detunes a few cents flatter than the last across the film, and any count past the true number gets an extra -100 cents and a dry, wrong-side pan.

From RECOUNT: UK call authenticity. Misdialled DTMF digits with real tone pairs and deletes, then 999 and the UK ringback cadence. The timer starts at connect. Scott's address appears as redaction bars or as no type at all.

From RECOUNT: 'Light reaches its hands, never its body.' Add the sixth hand on the sixth card as the first rung of a hand ladder: the same authored right-hand path appears as unrimmed ink pressing the card, then as a hole pressed into the blood, then as a hand of light on the grass.

From RECOUNT (optional, use sparingly): one second of POV through Marina's phone viewfinder just before the shutter. Four detection boxes lock onto the four silhouette heads, held by the steadiest hand in the room, then the flash. It keeps the doctrine because the Extra is never seen, only its view.

From RECOUNT: a deterministic secondary-motion method. Ponytail, curls and jacket hem are a pure function of t (a convolution of the past 12 frames of head and torso acceleration, or a re-simulation from shot start at fixed dt), not live spring state. Also adopt its per-scene OfflineAudioContext rendering and quarter-resolution halation extraction.

From ONE ROD TOO MANY: for the oven reveal, fold Christof's rig past its joint limits like a paper doll folded flat (limbs stacked at impossible angles), so the 18-frame silhouette reads as 'wrong body' instantly, not as an ambiguous ink mass.
must_fix: Honour 'Six hands come down on six cards. Angelo still holds the deck.' Show six hands. The sixth comes from the dark at Scott's right as unrimmed ink whose wrist never joins a body. Drop the 'five hands and a card flattening under nothing' version, which the characters would visibly notice.

Reconcile the hand-circle 'pentagon' with 'He is holding Angelo's hand. Of course he is.' The top-down should be a four-body ring where the Scott-Angelo link is stretched long over the empty seat and the fifth glass, a kink rather than a fifth person, so the close-up reveal stays true.

Actually stage the LATER game beat: 'Six piles now. Six people apparently playing', with Kay never in a clear view. Use the silhouette logic: an unrimmed figure is ink against ink, so 'Kay' is only rain-bead glints, a tucked-in chair, cards landing at her place and the lip-marked glass. This adds no positive Extra shape.
Change the VOICE typeface rule. The name-owner's face reads as people saying their own names. Use the mimicked speaker's face (see the grafts).

Type contrast rule: dialogue may only sit over ink or soot regions, or on an ink knock-behind. Tungsten type (Scott), ivory (Christof) and rain-silver (Kay) disappear over the tungsten light bands of the party scenes. Run a minimum-contrast check per line in the timeline linter.

Determinism: the damped springs (ponytail k70/c7, curls, jacket hem, word springs) cannot carry state between frames. Compute them in closed form or re-simulate from the shot's start at fixed dt on every render(t).

Store all character and set geometry as point and Bezier arrays, not opaque Path2D. Edge-noise displacement, shadow matrices, rim offsets, Deena's throat line and the shared right-hand path all need vertex access. Build Path2D per frame from that data.

Halation: Canvas 2D has no threshold operation. Draw the emissive elements (lamp cores, fire, glints, knockouts, bright type) into a separate quarter-resolution emissive buffer, blur it, tint it and composite it with 'screen'. Avoid full-resolution getImageData.

Audio: a single 14-minute stereo 48 kHz OfflineAudioContext is about 320 MB of float buffers. Render per scene with equal-power crossfades, from the same cue table as render(t), with seeded noise buffers.

Deena's throat: a ruler-straight ember line across the full width of a profile neck silhouette splits the shape and reads as decapitation. Make it a short arc across the front of the throat that stops before the nape: ember, then blood, within 4-8 frames, and under a second on first view.

Fast sections must let dialogue persist across cuts, anchored to the screen, not the shot. A 1.3 s kitchen average shot length cannot hold lines like 'Marina? Marina, get away from the door.' (about 2.3 s by the proposal's own hold rule).

Verbatim lint: generate the dialogue JSON directly from the screenplay and check every on-screen string against it. The proposal already shortens lines: 'I don't know. I don't know where-- I don't know.' and 'Kay! Save yourself. He's rearranged the whole room.' Decide once how '--' renders (an em dash), and confirm every face, including Six Caps and Abril Fatface, has the glyph.

Call-timer continuity: no timer while dialling (the keypad shot currently shows 00:01:12). Start at 00:00:00 on connect, never jump within a continuous shot, and land on 00:02:51 at 'Two.'. Keep the cold open at 00:03:24 deliberate, with the cropped-hand ember flicker supporting it.

Act 1 legibility: before production, build a silhouette lineup (each character identifiable in pure ink at 120 px tall) and a 60-second Act 1 test cut to prove the banter plays without faces. Test the 8 graphic-eye extreme close-ups for uncanniness and cut them if they fail.

Letterbox and type layout: at 2.39-2.76 the active frame is only about 696-800 px tall. Type size and placement rules must scale with the matte, and lines must never fall under it. Reserve the Dispatcher's fixed band and Scott's 160 px 'Me.' and 'Two.' within the live area of the yard compositions.

Photosensitivity pass: the explosion's white and inverted frames, the 4-6-frame cuts, the single-frame wine flashes and the strobe bars must be checked so there are no more than 3 full-frame luminance flashes per second. Fade between flash frames where they cluster.

Oven insert readability: an ink mass inside a lit box can read as just 'something dark'. Lead with the projected ceiling shadow. Separate the curl cloud, the bent knee and the palm-up hand with the oven-bulb rim. Fold the rig past its joint limits so the shape is unmistakably wrong within 18 frames.

scores.proposal_name: NEGATIVE SPACE: a cut-paper noir where the extra guest is the hole
scores.strengths: It is the only proposal whose rules match the roll-call geometry in the script. If the Extra sits at Scott's right, between Scott and Angelo, both VOICE lines ('Scott.' going left, 'Angelo.' going right) make sense, and every composition keeps that gap open. The visibility ladder (L0 to L8) builds slowly, the way the script does, instead of showing the trick on the first frame. The VOICE is the strongest treatment in the field. Its letters are knocked out to the ember lightbox, and every audio bus drops to digital silence for the word, so the presence is a hole in both picture and sound. There are seven type voices with four redundant cues each (face, colour, entrance behaviour, landing sound), backed by real readability rules: holds of max(0.8 s, 0.3 s + 55 ms per character), at most three lines on screen, entrances of 250 ms or less. Several type ideas act inside the world, not over it: the oven door slices 'Scott, don't--' in half; Christof's marquee bulbs fail on the joke that dies; Kay's last glyph lingers in lipstick red; Marina's mono grid shakes apart; Deena's crimson cursor dies on her almost-comment. Three counting devices are original and intense: the letterbox works as a headcount (1.85 to 2.76), the party groove gains a 7th beat after the second click, and the leitmotif is the 7th harmonic, one partial too many. Silhouettes remove the risk of procedural faces, and posterised light, rim crescents and frozen-then-boiling cut edges are a credible route to a premium look.
scores.weaknesses: It shows five hands pressing six cards, but the script says 'Six hands come down on six cards'. A card flattening under no hand is something the characters would react to. Angelo's 'not himself' voice (Oswald 300, lighter-cream, level) starts at the photo and kitchen, which takes away the script's explicit cue that 'Scott. Please.' is the first time. The VOICE borrows the face of the name it says, so 'Scott.' reads as Scott saying his own name, and that undercuts 'Didn't somebody already say me?' Scott's type (tungsten #F2A93B) and Marina's (ring-gold #D4AF5E) are almost the same colour, and the two share most of the late scenes. Dealing Angelo's words one at a time with tilt up to +/-9 degrees and overlaps is too slow for his long lines and hurts legibility. The 'six people apparently playing / Kay never in clear view' beat is missing, and staging it as a positive shape would break its own rule that the Extra is never a positive shape. Handedness is inconsistent: the handprint and the final hand are both a 'right hand', but the Extra stands at Scott's right. The look (Bass silhouette noir with ember orange) is the least novel of the three and shares its core hole idea with ONE ROD.

scores.proposal_name: RECOUNT: the night, rebuilt as evidence
scores.strengths: It has the best single dialogue idea in the field. Scott types with a caret and his lines are deleted backwards like a draft he won't send, which grows straight out of 'the text you started on Monday'. 'Two.' is the line that is never deleted. Its type rationales are the most story-grounded: each character's face is borrowed from an object they hold. Deena's yellow leader lines make her the in-world person who annotates the world. Angelo's card slugs have suit indexes and land face-down after Deena dies. Marina's wine ring drawn around 'live', and her last ring left hanging empty in the doorway, are excellent. The dormant 999 call line wakes during the oven scream with its waveform clipping red, so the scream becomes a picture. The address is shown as redaction bars instead of invented words. The HEADCOUNT irony (dropping 04 to 03 while everyone watches Angelo hold Deena) and the payoff where 'Two.' finally matches the record are genuinely new. The sound ideas are smart: the gas hiss is subliminal from the moment Christof leaves the table, and the count ticks drift 7 cents flatter each time.
scores.weaknesses: An omniscient, always-true HEADCOUNT plus labelled exhibits ('HANDS DEALT 7 · SEATED 6') over-explains a story built on uncertainty. It also states as fact that Kay and Marina are dead, which the script leaves open. Exhibit freezes, forensic tents, face-detection squares and a corner odometer risk a screen-life or UI-demo look, and they put the audience at a distance from Scott's subjective horror. Full-colour characters with skin tones, mouthless faces, three cross-faded head views and creased, nailed hands carry the highest uncanny and 'cheap procedural' risk of the three. The type colours collide badly: Scott and the Dispatcher are the same hex (#E6EEF5), and Marina, Angelo's cards and the VOICE are all card-stock white. A 35% scrim on every line, plus a transcript strip for the Dispatcher, drift toward plain subtitles. Six overprinted faces at 22% each, plus a 'SPEAKER: UNATTRIBUTED' tag, is clever but blurry and too literal. The blank card at 'Five. It's five.' contradicts the beat where that count is 'Perfect.'

scores.proposal_name: ONE ROD TOO MANY: a shadow theatre for seven
scores.strengths: It has the most original counting grammar. Visible rods follow an N+1 rule (wides let you count, close-ups are where things vanish), and there is one shot of the orphan rod in the photo ending where a camera would be held. The scrim is a single persistent object, so the Extra's punched-through VOICE letters accumulate on the walls and light the standoff 'like stars'. That is the best VOICE persistence idea. The VOICE borrows the face of whoever would say that same name ('Scott.' in Angelo's slab, echoing his line before he says it), which is the sharpest reading of 'a perfectly familiar voice'. Angelo's break lands exactly on 'Scott. Please.' (no card, thin ink), and 'Sorry about your house.' arrives face down and flips. Scott's variable-width type narrows with dread and releases on 'Two.' Christof's last line stays pinned to his empty chair. Kay is the only puppet animated on ones, and after she leaves, glimpses of 'Kay' snap on twos ('something else is wearing her timing'), which is a superb motion tell. The second heartbeat drifts into lockstep on 'Two.' Profile-only puppets with brass split pins are the most reliably buildable at high quality.
scores.weaknesses: A stage lip and rods in every wide make the film constantly about a puppet show, and the Over the Garden Wall / storybook warmth works against the 'so intense' brief. Two rods in the first frame reveal the Extra's existence immediately, and the bare rod never escalates. Rods also imply a puppeteer, a fatalistic layer the script doesn't have. Marina's lines are set around a circle, so long sentences wrap upside-down and hairline Bodoni at 44 px will not read at speed, which fails the readability requirement. Caveat, Anton and Alfa Slab are overused Google faces, and coloured plates on every line read like sticker labels. The Extra's geography (Scott's right) is never pinned down. The ending wide shows Scott's hand 'closed on empty air' with no hole, which contradicts 'THEIR HANDS, held tight' being visible. A 38-second take is too short for the standoff's roughly 20 lines and beats. Four single-frame white flash cuts inside 18 frames break photosensitivity flash limits.

winner: NEGATIVE SPACE: a cut-paper noir where the extra guest is the hole
grafts: From RECOUNT: Scott's lines type on with a caret and leave by deleting backwards, like the unsent Saturday text. Keep P1's guillotine for interrupted dashes. 'Two.' is the one Scott line that is never deleted, and his caret simply stops.

From RECOUNT: a dormant 1 px 999 call line along the bottom edge from the title onward. It wakes on the oven scream, its waveform clipping into the red, and that waveform is the scream. It becomes the full call in the yard.
From RECOUNT: the gas hiss starts subliminally (about -54 dBFS) the moment Christof leaves the table and rises until the kitchen, so 'Gas.' is a recognition, not a new sound.
From RECOUNT: count ticks (P1's glass-tick 'specular counts') go 7 cents flatter on every use across the film, so counting itself goes sour.

From RECOUNT: after Marina's grid line completes, a wine ring draws around its key word ('live'). After she vanishes, her last ring hangs empty in the kitchen doorway. This replaces P1's lone 'Marina?' floating in the rectangle.
From RECOUNT: 'Big night for you.' stays as an about-8% afterimage on the corridor wall in later hallway shots and dies when the procession passes the bathroom door.
From RECOUNT: the unwritten address appears as redaction bars in the Dispatcher's band, never invented words.

From RECOUNT: six hands come down on six cards. Five lead back to rim-lit bodies. The sixth's forearm comes out of the unlit ink beyond the lamp ring at Scott's right, which P1's silhouette world makes naturally ambiguous.

From ONE ROD: VOICE knockouts never heal. Each stays burned into the surface where it appeared (table, wall), so by the standoff the dark kitchen holds every word the Extra has said as faint ember holes.

From ONE ROD: the VOICE borrows the face of whoever would say that same name. The first 'Scott.' is in Angelo's Oswald, pre-echoing his line so his 'I just did' lands. The soft 'Angelo.' is in Scott's Franklin (his round-two line) or Deena's Archivo Black.

From ONE ROD: Kay alone animates on ones, with softer easing. After the bathroom click, every glimpse of 'Kay' at the later game snaps on twos and casts no shadow (P1's own shadow rule). This stages the missing 'six people apparently playing' beat without breaking the doctrine.
From ONE ROD: map Scott's dread to a variable-width axis (for example Archivo wdth 100 to 62) instead of tracking alone, and release it to full width on 'Two.'
From ONE ROD: Christof's last marquee, 'And don't touch my cards.', stays pinned to his empty chair-back with dead bulbs, and his biscuit stays on the table: the first things left behind.
From ONE ROD: whenever a count is wrong, Angelo deals one blank, wordless slot after his line, never acknowledged. It is conspicuously absent after the 'Perfect.' five-card deal.
From ONE ROD: in the yard a second heartbeat enters out of phase and drifts into lockstep with Scott's exactly on 'Two.'
From ONE ROD: shoot the lighter standoff as one unbroken push of about 50-60 s while P1's mattes squeeze continuously. The first cut is 'Scott runs.'
From ONE ROD: a whole-frame paper burn-through front (low-res fbm threshold with a char edge) for the explosion, layered with P1's negative-inversion frames and burning matte strips.
From ONE ROD: before building shots, run a silhouette identification sheet in which all six must be recognisable in pure ink at 120 px tall.
must_fix: The script says 'Six hands come down on six cards.' Show six hands, with the sixth arm dissolving into unlit ink at Scott's right. Do not show a card flattening under no hand, which the characters would visibly react to.

Key Angelo's full voice break to 'Scott. Please.', the script's explicit 'first time all night he hasn't sounded like himself'. Before that, degrade in stages: crooked dealing, then dropped words, then 'And Christof's in the kitchen.' undealt but still card blue. Lighter-cream, plain and level only from 'Scott. Please.' onward.

Replace the rule that the VOICE uses 'the face of the name it says'. As written, 'Scott.' reads as Scott saying his own name, which kills 'Didn't somebody already say me?' Use the face of the character who says that name in the roll call.

Separate the type colours. Scott's tungsten #F2A93B and Marina's ring-gold #D4AF5E are nearly identical and share most late scenes. Also check Kay's rain-silver, Christof's ivory and the Dispatcher's phone-white for confusion. Set a minimum colour difference on both ink and tungsten grounds.

Angelo's word-by-word dealing is too slow for long lines ('Are we doing this, then? Or did we all come here to hear Christof say "exposure" again?') and too skewed at +/-9 degrees with overlaps. Deal by phrase or sentence, and cap tilt on plot-critical lines so they stay level enough to read.

Stage the 'Six piles now. Six people apparently playing... she isn't visible in any clear, uninterrupted view' beat. It is absent from the sequence list. Resolve it within the never-a-positive-shape doctrine: fragments only, no cast shadow, wrong animation cadence.

Fix handedness and geography. The Extra is always at Scott's right, so the phone goes in his left hand at his left ear and the free right hand sits on the gap side in the cold open and the ending. The clasping hand must be a mirrored (left) version of the handprint path, or the choice must be justified on screen.

Several verbatim lines are missing from the sequence plans (for example 'There was-- something had her. I saw her hair--', 'Then how did it--', 'The cards. The picture. I thought I was--', 'And whoever did this just comes with us?', 'You always keep the back gate unlocked?', 'Four. There's four of us.'). Build a complete verbatim dialogue table and cut a type-only animatic to prove the hold rules fit the 14:00 runtime.

Make the call timer coherent: 00:00 at connect, the two dialling misses before it starts, 'Two.' at about 02:51, cold open at 03:24. Flag the cold-open-after-'Two.' loop as an interpretation to clear with the author.

Flash safety for an MP4 that will be shared: the blast-white frames, the inversion frames, four single-frame wine flashes, the camera flash and the red/blue strobe must stay under 3 flashes per second in any window, with saturated-red flashes limited. Run a Harding-style check.

Keep the 'at most four colours per shot' rule and simplify the 32-token palette. With the frame 40-92% ink, ember orange can slide into the generic dark-plus-orange look unless tungsten bands, the card blue and the type colours keep doing visible work.
Act 1 must be funny and warm in pure silhouette. Prove comic timing and speaker ID in a test of the arrivals and the 'Sit down, Scott' exchange before committing the 14 masters.
